subject: Geofence evidence, tenant evacuation scenarios, and handback timeline
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@finsecure.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request: evidence for region pinning + evacuation scenarios

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo. Our compliance team needs a concise package demonstrating how Redwood will satisfy our data locality and deletion requirements for a Dedicated deployment. Specifically:

- Evidence that tenant data can be pinned to a single geography (US-East) and will not replicate outside the pinned region.
- Documentation of the isolation model (network and storage boundaries) and an ops playbook for tenant evacuation (if we request decommission).
- Expected timeline for a full tenant wipe and an example of the wipe audit artifacts you can provide (logs, snapshots destroyed).

Can you share a short runbook and an example audit sample we can show auditors? Also note any constraints (backup replication windows, cross-region failover options) that would affect our acceptance criteria.

We need this by EOD Thu 25 Jun to keep our board schedule.

Best,
Marta
Compliance Manager, FinSecure

--
FinSecure (external)
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@finsecure.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T16:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for region pinning + evacuation scenarios

Marta — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front, and I attached a compact ops runbook plus an evacuation matrix for your auditors: region-binding-ops-runbook.pdf, evacuation-scenario-matrix.xlsx.

Summary:
- Region pinning: Dedicated tenants can be anchored to a customer-selected region (e.g., us-east-1). We run storage and compute within that boundary and disable cross-region snapshot replication for pinned tenants by default.
- Isolation: Network-level segmentation (VPC peering / private endpoints) plus tenant-scoped storage keys. Compute nodes are scheduled on tenant pools; control plane metadata is logically separated and stored in a hardened control plane (we can arrange restricted access).
- Evacuation / wipe timeline: Standard timeline is: trigger -> quiesce writes (minutes) -> snapshot finalization (~5–15 min depending on workload) -> cryptographic key revocation and metadata purge (minutes) -> background zeroing and shred of local disk according to device erase policy (hours depending on hardware). We provide an audit package with: final snapshot id, key rotation/revocation event, deletion job id, and storage node erase confirmations. Sample artifact: wipe-audit-sample.txt attached.

Constraints / caveats:
- If you enable cross-region failover for DR, we need to document the replication window; pinning is incompatible with automatic cross-region replication unless explicitly configured for dual-write scenarios.
- Backups retained in long-term archival buckets (if you opt in) may require a separate retention policy; we can include a legal hold workflow if needed.

Next steps: Laura (ops) and Ben (security) are looped in to confirm wipe artifact format and to run a short proof-of-evidence run in our staging environment scoped to your tenant.

I can schedule a 30m run-through tomorrow to walk your compliance team through the artifacts. Is 10am PT possible?

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@finsecure.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-22T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for region pinning + evacuation scenarios

Marta — adding a few operational clarifications and a short checklist we will run during the staged proof:

- Proof scope: we will perform a tenant-bound wipe in our staging cluster that mirrors your config (pinned us-east-1, no cross-region backups). The run will produce: wipe job log, KV cache purge log, final snapshot marker, and storage node erasure confirmations.
- Timing expectations: for a 1TB tenant active steady-state, full confirmation (including zeroing/shred confirmation from NVMe) typically completes within 6–12 hours in our staging infra; the audit package is available immediately once the job completes (we email JSON artifacts and a signed run summary).
- Evidence format: we deliver a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums), job IDs, and node-level timestamps. We do not share raw disk images; we provide destruction confirmation and checksums.
- Legal hold interplay: if FinSecure requires legal holds, we will flag the tenant as \"hold\" which pauses deletion; revoking hold is a manual process requiring formal approval.

I'll plan the staged run for Thu 24 Jun at 10:00 PT unless you prefer a different time. Vivek — can you confirm we have staging capacity and the test tenant created? Ben, please confirm the artifact signing approach (KMS key to sign manifests).

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Manager, Cloud Ops — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@finsecure.com>

Quick update on signing and evidence hygiene:

- We'll sign the manifest with a customer-scoped key derived from our KMS and include the public key fingerprint in the manifest so FinSecure's auditors can validate the signature.
- The wipe-audit-sample.txt attached to Vivek's email is a sanitized example — the real run will include tenant-specific IDs.
- I'll produce a brief verification checklist that maps each artifact to an auditor question (e.g., \"How do you prove no cross-region replication?\" -> final snapshot metadata showing region tag + replication_disabled flag).

Vivek — we have staging capacity for Thu 24 Jun 10:00 PT. Aditya, can you ensure the staging tenant mirrors FinSecure's retention flags (no archival retention, replication disabled)?

Ben
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Team — thanks for quick turnaround and for scheduling the proof. We ran the artifacts past our internal auditors this morning and have two follow-ups before the run:

1) Can you include sample timeline metrics for larger tenants (5TB, 20TB) — particularly the range for snapshot finalization + disk erase so we can log expected RTO/RPO during decommission?
2) In the manifest, please include the KMS key fingerprint and the signing certificate chain as a downloadable item. Our auditors will want to verify chain-of-custody.

If you can add those to the runbook or bring them to Thu's session, we should be set to mark this as accepted.

Appreciate it —
Paul
Head of Compliance Programs, FinSecure
